summary.text: Jerry Carl is a Mobile-born entrepreneur who served on the Mobile County Commission (2012-2020) and represented Alabama's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2021 to 2025. He lost the 2024 Republican primary to fellow incumbent Barry Moore after redistricting placed them in the same district, and won the 2026 Republican primary for the seat Moore vacated. According to his campaign website, he is running as an ally of President Trump on immigration, gun rights and reduced federal spending.

paragraphs.text: Born in Mobile, Alabama (June 17, 1958); graduated from Sylacauga High School in 1977 and attended Lake City Community College (now Florida Gateway College) before returning to Mobile, according to Wikipedia.
Worked for Alabama Power and as a salesman for several Mobile companies, and in 1989 established Stat Medical, a healthcare equipment business, according to Wikipedia.

According to his campaign website, started his first company at age 25 and has started more than ten companies, ranging from real estate to healthcare, timber and church-furniture manufacturing. Wikipedia lists Carl and Associates (a management group, 2003) and Cricket and Butterfly, LLC (lumber and timber).
Elected to the Mobile County Commission in 2012 after defeating incumbent Mike Dean in the Republican primary; re-elected in 2016 and chosen commission president in 2019, serving until 2020.

Won the 2020 Republican nomination for Alabama's 1st District, vacated by Bradley Byrne, in a runoff against former state senator Bill Hightower, then won the general election with 64.4% against Democrat James Averhart. Re-elected in 2022.
In the U.S. House (January 2021-January 2025), served on the Armed Services and Natural Resources committees in the 117th Congress and on Appropriations and Natural Resources in the 118th.
After the Allen v. Milligan redistricting put him and Rep. Barry Moore in the same district, lost the March 5, 2024 Republican primary to Moore by 3.4 points, according to Wikipedia.
Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary for the open seat with 74.6% of the vote, defeating Austin Sidwell, John Mills and Lucas Burger.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Tina, have been married 44 years and have three children and several grandchildren, and he describes himself as an avid hunter.
